chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn 'Ammar, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: A man came to a woman and asked her to marry him to herself. She said: I will marry you to myself on the condition that you seek from me whatever you wish of looking or seeking pleasure, and you attain from me what a man attains from his wife, except that you do not insert your private part into my private part, and you enjoy yourself with whatever you wish, for I fear disgrace. He said: 'He has from her only that which was stipulated.'

key_terms.تُزَوِّجَهُ نَفْسَهَا: She marries him to herself (offers herself in marriage)
key_terms.فَرْجَكَ فِي فَرْجِي: Your private part into my private part

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on a wife stipulating the exclusion of vaginal intercourse in the marriage contract?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *al-shartu min al-umma min al-haqq* (conditions are as stipulated) in Shia jurisprudence, where specific exclusions in the marriage contract override general rights. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that if a woman explicitly excludes vaginal intercourse (*al-dukhul*) to avoid pregnancy or social stigma, the husband is restricted to the agreed-upon pleasures, demonstrating the flexibility of marital contracts in Shi'a fiqh. This ruling underscores the importance of mutual consent and precise stipulation in defining the scope of conjugal rights.
